video.title: Jev explained in 7min..
video.genre: AI explainer and opinion, partly screen-shared

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Hook: 'one area that always felt short was workflow automation' -- even Astra and Fable can't cross that threshold. TypeSafe's claim: frontier models are optimized for the wrong thing (human preference, verifiable reward), which doesn't carry over when decisions must be quick under uncertainty; lands at 81.8. Two endings both work: the later one (108.7, L011-L013) adds the sharper 'forcing chat/agent models into automation is fundamentally wrong', at the cost of partly restating.

Hook: the Jev projects people show off are about speed of execution, not depth of understanding. Current LLMs can do the same tasks, just not at 70-500ms, because autoregressive decoding is token-by-token while Jev does parallel sampling and typed probabilistic decisions; lands at 162.3. The 'so it's less about capability than optimization' wrap-up to 176.6 is acceptable but restates the hook.

Hook: unlike LLMs that take an instruction and answer in text, Jev takes structured input and returns a probability distribution -- 'okay, what do I do with this?' Answer: three primitives (choice, score, yes/no) that software builds on; payoff line 'it almost feels like we're back to logic gates and registers'. One 'looks something like this' screen reference at ~268 but the point is spoken.

Closing hot take: the Jev news is about use cases growing horizontally, not novelty -- narrow specialized models existed before generative AI took over the narrative, and it's a net positive to build models optimized for the right constraints. Starts at 'how I process this' (drops 'So'). Two starts genuinely work: 374.3 adds the supporting evidence (TypeSafe hasn't disclosed RLCD; someone on Reddit built a similar 421M-param BERT model) for a 57s clip; preferred is the shorter one, which stands on its own.

negatives.why: Strong opening line ('Jev makes us question how we optimize LLMs') but followed by generic history of chat/coding optimization and the 'AI stack' pressure; the point doesn't arrive until the workflow-automation claim at 43s.
Sponsor read (Junie CLI from JetBrains): benchmark score, plan mode, discount.
Plant-sorting example narrated off the screen ('this long list of plants').
Pareto-frontier chart narration ('this section here'): model names and positions read off a plot.
